video_title: Portland Ran Away From Phoenix — Is This Blazers Team for Real?

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye on Portland's preparation and Phoenix's lack of readiness
quotes.excerpt: Portland was prepared, they were engaged and they were emotionally invested. On the other end, Phoenix seemed like they were not ready to play basketball.
quotes.quote: Obviously Richard and I are Phoenix people. I will say Portland was prepared, they were engaged and they were emotionally invested. On the other end, Phoenix seemed like they were not ready to play basketball, which is wild for a first game of the year. I think they were down 35 to 3 or something like that. That is hard when you have had preseason, you have had all these things, training camp, and you go into a game and throw out a flat tire like that. You are looking around like, what are we even going to work on? Everything? Yes.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye on Ja Morant's performance and smart team play
quotes.excerpt: He let the game come to him. He was not really forcing anything.
quotes.quote: One thing that I really appreciate about Ja that first game, he let the game come to him. He was not really forcing anything. People are going to take away that he does not have as much bounce as he used to, and that happens. But I thought that he was making the right play. I thought Danny Abdi was making the right play, Dame was making the right play. I thought that team played really, really smart. I thought Portland played smart, they played unselfish, and defensively, they were just making it hell for the other team.

quotes.speaker: Richard Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye and Richard Jefferson on early season overreactions
quotes.excerpt: You don't give out grades on the first day of school.

text_blocks.speaker: Channing Frye
text_blocks.text: Do you know who the leading scorer in the league is right now?

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: You don't give out grades on the first day of school. You saw what happened with Boston, it was a 23-0 run. You see a lot of these teams, ups, downs. Bad teams don't know they are bad yet. Ty Jerome goes and drops. That is true. That is why we talk about sample size. You are going to see these crazy numbers, these crazy swings, new players, new teams, new coaches, new system. You are going to see a little bit of chaos in the first 10, 12 games, then things start settling in. That is why around 20 games you give yourself, okay, do we need shooting? Are we banged up? Do we need more size? What does our defense look like? How do we adjust our offense?
